title: Stoker metadata — shared definitions
description: Types every document of the metadata repository uses. Not a document of its own. Enum values are camelCase names, never the numbers a program stores: a public format outlives the order of anybody's enum.

schemaVersion.description: `<major>.<minor>`: the version of the format a document was written for. v1 is still being developed and may change until the first recipe is published; from then on a minor version only adds — fields, enum values, kinds — and never changes what an existing field means, so a reader of an older minor reads a newer document of the same major. It ignores fields it does not know, and a value it does not know in a field that only describes (a provider, a tag kind, a store id kind, a definition's origin) it treats as absent; an entry for a platform it does not know is not for this host. Something it does not know that would change what is done to an install — a fix role, a step kind — it never skips silently: it treats that build as needing a newer reader. A reader refuses a major it does not know.

uuid.description: A UUID in its lowercase hyphenated form. Ids are minted once, by whoever first adds the thing to the repository, and never change: a rename keeps the id.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the bytes, lowercase hex.

blake3.description: BLAKE3-256 of the bytes, lowercase hex.

relativePath.description: A path inside an install, relative to its root, with forward slashes. No leading slash or `~`, no backslash, no `:` (a drive, or an NTFS stream), no control character, no empty, `.` or `..` segment: the same rule the launcher applies before it touches a player's disk.

fileName.description: A bare file name: no slashes, no `:`, no control character, not `.` or `..`.

expandedString.description: A string the installing machine fills in. `%INSTALLDIR%` becomes the install's root folder, in the machine's own form (`C:\Games\Example` on Windows, `/home/me/Games/Example` elsewhere), without a trailing separator; `%%` is a literal `%`. Any other `%` is refused, so a value copied from somewhere with a placeholder of its own (`%APPDATA%`, `50%`) fails here rather than reaching a player's machine unexpanded.

launchKey.description: A launch by its key — stable where its display name is not: names get translated and reworded. One key may stand for a launch on each platform (`play` on Windows and on Linux).

languageTag.description: A BCP 47 language tag in its canonical casing — language, optional script, optional region: `en`, `de`, `pt-BR`, `zh-Hans`, `es-419`. One spelling per language, so `pt-BR` and `pt-br` are never two keys of one text. Stores name languages their own way (Steam's `english`, GOG's `en-US`); the exporter maps them, so a reader never has to know any store's list.

localizedText.description: One text in one or more languages, keyed by language tag. Plain text, paragraphs separated by a blank line; no HTML. Most entries hold `en` alone because that is what the stores were asked for — more languages are additions, not a different shape.

partialDate.description: A date as precisely as it is known: `2017`, `2017-02`, `2017-02-24`. Stores publish bare years and months, and padding them to the first of January would invent a fact.

provider.description: Where something came from: a store, or a database about games. `eshop` is Nintendo's (via titledb), `community` a contributor's own work.

storeKey.description: A store by its key: `steam`, `gog`, `epic`, `ubisoft`, `ea`, `amazon`, `battlenet`, `humble`, `itchio`, `zoomplatform`, `eshop` — umu-database's names, with `epic` for its `egs` and `eshop` for Nintendo's. A key nobody has defined yet is allowed and kept: a reader ignores a store it does not know.

storeIdKind.description: What kind of id a store id is, in that store's vocabulary (the README's table). **Reported** kinds are what a game's store SDK asks about, and what an install reports as owned: Steam `appId`; GOG `productId`; Epic `catalogItemId` (`EOS_Ecom_QueryOwnership`) and `entitlementName` (`EOS_Ecom_QueryEntitlements`); Ubisoft `productId`; eShop `titleId`. **Identity** kinds are what imports match by and a store's API addresses things by, never reported: Steam `packageId`, `depotId`; GOG `galaxyClientId`; Epic `appName`, `namespace`, `offerId`. A minor version adds kinds; a reader ignores one it does not know.

id.description: Always a string, numeric ids too — quoted in YAML — so every store's ids have one shape and no reader parses a 64-bit id into a float.

label.description: Which id this is, for a person: "Standard edition", "Steam edition", "Pre-order bonus item". A store that numbers editions, bundles and the items inside them separately gives an item many ids; the label is how they are told apart.

storeEntry.description: One store's ids for one item — a game, a DLC or an edition — and which of them an install reports as owned. Never synthesised: a made-up AppId is indistinguishable from a real one and, the first time it reaches anything that talks to Valve, means a different game.

installed.description: Which of the reported-kind ids an install reports as owned: `all` of them, or only the ones listed, each as `<kind>:<id>`. An empty list reports none: the ids are known, and none is to be claimed. Identity kinds are never reported, whatever is said here. A game's ids are reported by every install of it, a DLC's by an install that carries it, an edition's by an install that carries every DLC it includes.

storeIds.description: Every store's ids for one item, by store key. How anybody holding a copy from a store finds its entry, so a `(store, kind, id)` belongs to one item in the whole repository — except kinds several items share by nature, such as Epic's `namespace`.

source.description: Provenance: which provider a value was read from, and where. Kept so a value can be fetched again and checked, never to be served to players.

retrieved.description: The day it was read. A day, not a timestamp, so re-reading an unchanged value the same day is no diff.

definitionOrigin.description: Where an achievement, stat or leaderboard definition came from. `observed`: Stoker saw a running game use it and nobody has described it since — worth finding and completing. `curated`: written by a contributor.

platform.description: One operating system or console. The desktop and mobile systems run a build directly; every other value is a console, run through an emulator.

architecture.description: The instruction set a build's binaries are for. `any` is the honest answer when nothing determined it.

runtimeKey.description: A shared runtime by its stable key — `vcredist-14-x64`, `directx-jun2010`. Runtimes are described once, in the repository's own catalogue, never per game.

pluginKey.description: A plugin's identity: the reverse-DNS id its manifest declares (`org.example.filename-redirect`), or for a .NET assembly its name in lower case (`bepinex.core`).

pluginVersion.description: Three or four numbers, optionally a pre-release suffix: `1.2.0`, `3.1.0.5`, `0.0.0-legacy`. No build metadata (`+…`), because a version is also a file name.

pluginRef.description: A plugin of a plugin registry (`https://schemas.stokerhq.app/plugins/v1/`) — a hook plugin, a mod loader, a mod, a library — pinned to one version. Pinned, because a newer version must never change what an existing entry installs. By key and version only, never by where the catalogue is kept, so the catalogue can live in a repository of its own.

downloads.description: Where the file's publisher offers it, in order of preference. Never a copy somebody else made: the repository redistributes nobody's binaries. Whatever comes back is checked against the file's hash, which alone decides whether it is the file; when every link is dead, an administrator supplies the file by hand and the hash still decides.

archive.description: When the URL serves an archive the file is inside: its format and the file's path in it.

pluginAssignment.description: A plugin from a plugin registry applied to a game, a release or one build, with the copies it is for — a hook plugin a loader runs inside the game, a mod laid into it. Placed and combined exactly as fixes and hooks are (the README's combine rule): written at the widest level it holds for, narrowed by `when`, switched off below by an assignment of the same plugin with `enabled: false`. Pinned to one version, so one release can keep a version while a later one moves on.

when.description: The copies the plugin is for. Absent: every copy the assignment is listed for.

atLaunch.description: The plugin has to be in place before the game's own code runs — it patches or catches something the game does at start, before it would load the library a plugin is otherwise loaded beside. A reader then starts the game with its plugins already loaded, as it does for a hook with `atLaunch`.

enabled.description: False on a release or a build: switches off the assignment of the same plugin from a level above for those copies.

config.description: The plugin's options, checked against the configuration contract its manifest declares.

archiveRef.description: A file kept in the presentation archive (`StokerHQ/Archive`), by its SHA-256 — never the bytes. The archive stores every file once under its hash, with where it came from; descriptions, artwork, screenshots and achievement icons are archived so they outlive the store pages they came from, and kept apart from the recipes so a request to remove one picture removes one archived file and leaves every recipe as it was. A reader fetches the file from an archive mirror and checks the hash; when no mirror has it, from `source.url`.

archiveFields.description: What every archive reference has; `archiveRef`, `archiveImage` and an archived text close it.

contentType.description: `image/webp`, `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`; `text/plain; charset=utf-8` for a description in plain text (paragraphs separated by a blank line); `text/html; charset=utf-8` for a long description kept as its store publishes it, which a reader sanitises before showing.

source.description: Where the archived bytes were taken from, and when — what lets a file be traced, fetched again, and removed precisely if its owner asks.

archiveImage.description: An archived picture, with its pixel size so a reader can lay it out before fetching it.

localizedArchiveText.description: One archived text in one or more languages, keyed by language tag: each language's text is its own archived file.

localizedArchiveDescription.description: A long description in one or more languages, each its own archived file: plain text, or HTML as the store publishes it — Steam's and GOG's are HTML, with lists, headings and the media they embed. HTML is kept as published and sanitised by a reader before it is shown.

presentation.description: What a store page shows of a game, a DLC or an edition — its words and pictures — archived (`archiveRef`) rather than written here. The facts about it (developers, publishers, release date) are in the item's `storePage`; nothing here changes what is done to an install, so a reader that shows nothing ignores the whole block.

description.description: Unbounded: Steam's run past 9,000 characters, and an archived file has no cap that would decide how much of a real description is lost.

artwork.description: The slots a library draws an item with, by the names Steam's library cache uses.

capsule.description: Portrait box art, 2:3 (600×900 on Steam) — what a library grid shows.

header.description: The wide store header (460×215 on Steam).

hero.description: The wide banner behind a game's page.

logo.description: The transparent wordmark laid over the hero.

icon.description: The small square icon a store or a desktop shortcut uses.

reel.description: Screenshots and trailers in the order the store page shows them — for Steam every trailer in its order, then every screenshot in its order.

oneOf.description: A trailer. Video is kept by reference: its source and the hash of each track as a reader stores it (fragmented MP4), not in the archive — tens of megabytes each make it a question of storage, not of format.

highlight.description: The store marks it as one to lead with; recorded, never used to reorder.

sourceKey.description: The store's own id for the trailer, so a re-import recognises it.

track.description: One track of a trailer as a reader stores it: fragmented MP4.

contentFingerprint.description: What a set of files is, independent of where it is stored. An instance computes it from its own manifest and finds a repository build by it, so one entry describes the same files wherever they were ingested. The files themselves are never in the repository.

algorithm.description: `stoker-tree-1`: BLAKE3-256 over the UTF-8 text made of one line per file — `<path>\t<size>\t<blake3>\n`, path relative and forward-slashed, size in decimal bytes, the file's BLAKE3 in lowercase hex — ordered by path, ordinal. Empty directories do not count. The per-file BLAKE3 is the one every Stoker manifest already holds.

marker.description: One file that identifies a build even when the copy around it has changed. A copy a player had on disk has written its configs, saves and logs into the folder, or has a patch applied, so its fingerprint matches nothing; its executables and main data files usually still do. BLAKE3, because every Stoker manifest already holds it per file.

fileCheck.description: One file of an install as it has to be: there with these bytes, or not there at all.

fixCondition.description: What a copy has to be for a fix or a plugin to be for it. Every part given has to hold: each file as stated, one of the platforms, one of the architectures, a release in the range. A fix or a plugin is written once, at the widest level it holds for, and narrowed here — never copied into every release. Never by store: a copy is its files, so where two stores' copies need different things their files differ, and a file check or a build of its own says so.

releases.description: Which releases of the game, by release id, compared by the releases' `order`: from `from` (included) up to `before` (not included), or exactly the ones in `only`. A release added later inside a range is covered without an edit. A copy that matches no release of the repository holds no release condition.

fix.description: One thing that is done to a copy so it runs, or that a player can choose to have done: a patch, a mod, a language, the publisher's own setup. An ordered list of steps, applied together or not at all. Fixes are applied in order — a build's own first, then its release's, then its game's, each list in its order — and each fix's `when` is checked against the files as they are when its turn comes.

id.description: Stable, so a release or a build can switch the fix off and a report can name it.

role.description: `setup`: the publisher's own install steps. `languagePack`: what a language needs. `patch`: a fix — a community patch, a publisher hotfix, a compatibility tweak. `mod`: content somebody added. There is no DLC role: how a DLC reaches a copy depends on where the copy came from.

name.description: What a person reads in a list: "German", "Widescreen fix".

language.description: For a `languagePack`: the language it is (BCP-47) — what Stoker picks a pack by from the player's language. Required there, and not given on any other role.

when.description: The copies the fix is for. Absent: every copy it is listed for. A fix whose `when` does not hold is not for this copy and is left out — which is how one fix written against an executable's bytes serves every copy, from every store or disk, that has those bytes.

appliedWhen.description: What shows the fix is already in place, so a copy somebody patched by hand is not patched twice.

optional.description: The copy works without it, so a player may leave it out. Not optional means applied whenever its `when` holds.

default.description: An optional fix, or one answering a question, that is chosen unless somebody says otherwise.

available.description: False for a fix that cannot produce a working install — kept, with its reason, so nobody offers it again. Assassin's Creed declares six languages, and Russian installs no executable.

enabled.description: False to keep the finding without applying it.

links.description: Where the fix is documented or comes from, for a person reading the entry.

gameFix.description: A fix listed on a game or a release rather than on one build: a patch or a mod for whichever copies its `when` holds for.

step.description:
One thing a fix does. Most change the install once, when the fix is applied; `environment`, `arguments` and `windowsCompatibility` apply every time the game starts. A minor version adds kinds; a reader that meets one it does not know treats the build as needing a newer reader rather than leave the step out. `run`, `firewall`, `registry` and `environment` reach beyond the install's own files, so a contributor's step is held to the install (see each); only a step read from the publisher's own install script (`source`) may go further, because the publisher's installer would have done the same.

Every step kind has a class, `x-stokerhq-class` on its definition: `unattended` steps a reader may apply on its own, `optIn` steps only with the player's consent for that fix — they run programs, write outside the install's files, or change executable bytes. Every reader draws the line in the same place.

filesStep.description: Lay a set of files over the install; a path both have is replaced. The files are named by fingerprint — never stored here.

into.description: The folder they go into. Absent: the install root.

downloadStep.description: Fetch one file from where its publisher offers it, check it by hash, and lay it into the install — an archive's contents instead of the archive when `extract` is given. How a mod, a community server or a tool that is published as a release gets into an install without the repository holding a byte of it: the file is the publisher's, exactly as published. `optIn`: it brings somebody else's code into the install.

file.description: The file as its publisher offers it. Whatever a link returns is checked against `sha256`, which alone decides whether it is the file; when every link is dead, a player supplies the file by hand and the hash still decides.

extract.description: The file is an archive; lay what is in it. Absent: the file itself is laid into `into`.

from.description: The folder in the archive whose contents are taken — a release's own top folder, `Peacock-v8.10.1`. Absent: the archive's root.

exclude.description: Paths below `from` that are not laid. Leave a published file out only when it would get in the way; one that is merely unused stays, so the install holds the release as published.

into.description: The folder it goes into. Absent: the install root.

result.description: What the step lays down, as it lands — paths from the install root. A reader checks it after the step, and one that already holds these files (a store of its own) may lay them without fetching.

deleteStep.description: Remove files — an intro video that crashes, a launcher stub that must not run. A path that is not there is not an error.

iniSetStep.description: Set one key of an INI-style file, creating the file, section and key when they are missing and keeping everything else as it was.

hexEditStep.description: Change bytes of one file in place — the shape most widescreen and FOV fixes are published in. Each edit checks the bytes it replaces and refuses a file that has others there; the fix's `when` says which file, by hash, the offsets are for.

from.description: The bytes found there, lowercase hex.

to.description: The bytes written, lowercase hex; as many as `from`.

binaryPatchStep.description: Turn one file into another with a binary diff. The diff is named by hash, never stored here.

fromBlake3.description: The file before; any other is refused.

toBlake3.description: The file after; a result that hashes otherwise is discarded.

installScriptSource.description: The install script (one of the build's `installScripts`) a step was read from. Absent for a step a contributor added.

registryStep.description: Write one registry value. Windows only. A contributor's step writes only below the game's own key — `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\<vendor>\…` or `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\<vendor>\…` (`WOW6432Node` allowed), never under `Microsoft`, `Classes`, `Policies`, `RegisteredApplications` or `Clients`, which is where autostarts, file associations and policy live. A step read from an install script (`source`) writes what the publisher's installer would have.

key.description: The full key, hive included, spelt out: `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Publisher\Game`.

language.description: The language the value is written for; absent for every language.

enabled.description: False to keep a step read from a script without carrying it out.

firewallStep.description: Let one program through Windows Firewall. Windows only. A contributor's step names a program inside the install; only a step read from an install script (`source`) may name one elsewhere.

name.description: The rule's name, which Windows shows in its list.

runStep.description: Run a program once the files are in place (`run`) or before they are removed (`runOnUninstall`): the publisher's own setup step, or a fix's patcher. Off by default for an `.exe` with no switches, which would put a UI in front of the player. A contributor's step runs a program inside the install — one a `files` step laid there, typically; only a step read from an install script (`source`) may run one elsewhere.

hasRunKey.description: Where Steam records having run it.

environmentStep.description: Set an environment variable every time the game starts. Not one that makes a runtime load code the variable names (`LD_PRELOAD`, `DYLD_*`, `COR_PROFILER`, `DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS`, `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` and their kind): code a fix needs goes into the install, where a hash says what it is.

mode.description: `set` replaces the variable. `prepend` and `append` add to a list such as `PATH`, joined with the machine's list separator (`;` on Windows, `:` elsewhere) — and simply set it when it is empty.

launch.description: Only for this launch. Absent: every launch.

argumentsStep.description: Add arguments to the command line every time the game starts, after the launch's own.

launch.description: Only for this launch. Absent: every launch.

windowsCompatibilityStep.description: Start one executable under Windows compatibility layers — `WINXPSP3`, `HIGHDPIAWARE`, `DISABLEDXMAXIMIZEDWINDOWEDMODE` — as the Compatibility tab would. Windows only.

hook.description: One declarative hook on a DLL's named export: return a value instead, forward to it, or call it and look at — or override — its result; optionally rewrite one string argument. Placed on a game, a release or a build and combined like fixes and plugins (the README's combine rule): written at the widest level it holds for, narrowed by `when`, switched off below by `disableHooks`. A reader that applies hooks applies at most 16 to one copy, the most its loader takes.

id.description: Stable, so a release or a build can switch the hook off (`disableHooks`) and a report can name it.

when.description: The copies the hook is for. Absent: every copy it is listed for.

atLaunch.description: The hook has to be in place before the game's own code runs — it catches something the game does at start, before it would load the library the hook lives beside. A reader then starts the game with its hooks already loaded.

behavior.description: `return` skips the original; `forward` tail-calls it; `intercept` calls it and observes the result.

value.description: Signed 32-bit forced or override result; sign-extended on x64.

override.description: Intercept only: substitute `value` for the result.

param.description: 1-based index of a string argument to rewrite; 0 disables rewriting.

wide.description: The string is UTF-16 rather than narrow ASCII.

guards.description: Guards on arguments' low 32 bits; all must match before the string is read.
